method: Own script scripts/recompute.py, written from PROTOCOL.md alone (analyze.py was not read or imported), run on the extracted committed tarball. For each (q, seed) and pass: ratio = sum over DL attempt records of relations.cpu (ARM) / same (REF); pass-mean = arithmetic mean of the two pass ratios; floor = max |REF2/REF - 1| over the 4 single-pass and 2 pass-mean A/A values; SUPPORTED iff all 15 pass-means and all 30 single-pass ratios < 1 - floor. Total CPU = DL record sum over the 7 phases' .cpu; RSS from the rss record. Every numeric entry of analysis.json (157 values) was compared with the recompute: 0 differences beyond 1e-12 relative.

problems.issue: Whole-process CPU falls far less than the DL phase sum. Replay (ABBA mean of pairs, 5 units, k = 20-22): process CPU (wait4 utime+stime) COMBO/REF 0.899-0.962, a 4-10% saving (0.962 at k = 22). The producer's own unit wall_ms ratios give 0.932-0.980 geomean per size (0.935 at k = 22). Over the same runs the DL-record phase sum falls to 0.783-0.842 in the replay and to 0.796-0.884 geomean per size in the producer data (0.796 at k = 22), and relations.cpu to about 0.43-0.56. The 'total CPU about 0.80' figure is the DL pipeline as PROTOCOL.md defines it. It must not be read as the end-to-end process saving, which also pays for the instance search and the D and DL1 arms.

The 'total CPU at k = 22 about 0.80' is the DL record's phase sum (fb, relations, matrix, linear_algebra, log_recovery, descent, verify), as PROTOCOL.md defines it. It excludes the instance search (search_s in the ratios record, 0.2-35 s depending on q and seed), the D and DL1 arms' own linear algebra and the calibration. End to end, the process CPU ratio COMBO/REF in this replay is 0.90-0.96 (0.962 at k = 22, seed 8). The producer's own unit wall_ms ratios give 0.93-0.98 geomean per size (0.935 at k = 22). Neither contradicts the protocol metric, but the whole-process saving is about 4-10%, not about 20%.

Replayed DL-record total CPU at k = 22 (one unit, seed 8, ABBA mean of pairs) is 0.827, against the claimed geomean of 0.796 over seeds 1-3. That lies inside the producer's own range of 0.71-0.87. Total CPU is noisy on this host (the study's A/A total-CPU pairs were 0.85-1.11).

The study's 20.7% floor is set by one slow REF unit (p2 REF q=2097091 seed 1: relations.cpu 2.2818 s, against 1.9328 s in p1 and 1.8096 s for p2 REF2), and reproduces exactly. COMBO clears it in every cell and pass (worst single 0.6439 < 0.7931). The replay's A/A at q=2097091 seed 9 is 0.983 (1.7%), and the spread over its 4 REF runs is 9.6% max/min.

benchmarks/records/20261114T2208Z-ic-gw-fasthash.json has raw[0].uploaded = false: the raw tarball is not in S3, although the bench.record rule requires it. It is in git, which is what made the recompute possible.
README embeds fasthash.png, which commit 8da2fac152 moved to the artifact store (.artifacts.json pins sha256 119a78df...). The validator did not fetch or check it. No headline depends on it.

The README's 'HASH probably a real gain at k >= 21' is labelled post hoc and is not validated as a claim. The frozen-rule HASH decision NOT SUPPORTED reproduces: four single-pass values are at or above 1 - floor, and q=1048507 seed 2 pass 1 is 1.0629 > 1.

Apart from the A/A null, the protocol pre-registers no negative case, such as a size where the chain gain should vanish. Post hoc, COMBO is weakest at q=524287 (geomean 0.545), where the chain saves least (chain_cost 17 vs plain_cost 18, a single segment). This is consistent with the mechanism but is not evidence.

L0: shared session container (4 vCPU, Intel Xeon 2.10 GHz), no CPU isolation, no Iso Lab EKS route, no native L2/replay/A/A admission. CPU seconds are a within-session paired comparison only; CPU only (no GPU, no other microarchitecture). Wall/CPU time is not a measured bound (AGENTS.md, 'Curve identity and measured bounds') and moves no counted-cost frontier.

Counted work is identical by the gate, so the counted M-eq and the gap to the matched rho are unchanged. This validation supplies no rho reference or §5a band. A VALIDATION.json for any leaderboard or benchmarks row would still need a matched rho reference.

The replay covers 7 of the 45 (q, seed) units in the universe (2 of them also in the producer's 15); timing replay covers 5 units at k = 20-22 with one ABBA block each and one A/A pair. Seeds 4-9 are new instances of the same family, not new curve families.
Validated snapshot a851708714. Remote main had moved to 6ef2197cf9 at nonce time; it was not fetched, so later changes to the study directory are not covered.

Independence: the validator is a subagent of the producer's Claude Code session on the same container. It used its own scripts and builds and did not read analyze.py or plot.py. The REF binary was taken from the scratchpad path the task card named (hash-verified and rebuilt bit-identically from the published sources).

A passed report means the receipt is admissible evidence for the COMBO time-only claim at k = 18..22 in this family and setting. It does not support an ECDLP claim or demonstrate any asymptotic speedup, and it does not authorize promotion or a leaderboard row.
